topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecture, outlining its learning outcomes and framing the discussion of cancer progression and hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal deregulation and oncogenic signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell surface receptors and intracellular signaling cascades confer growth signal autonomy and survival.

topics.label: Blocks to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells fail to undergo normal terminal differentiation using examples from hematopoiesis and the intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how alterations in p53 and Bcl-2 family proteins allow cancer cells to resist apoptotic cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomeres, and cellular stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how telomere shortening triggers senescence and how cancer cells bypass stress checkpoints and reactivate telomerase to achieve immortalization.

topics.label: Cancer metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce complex cancer hallmarks and explain how tumor cells alter cellular metabolism, including the Warburg effect and oncometabolite signaling.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how growing tumors overcome nutrient and oxygen limits by stimulating new blood vessel formation.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the multi-step metastatic cascade, the use of circulating tumor cells for monitoring, and the genomic features of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks conclude the lecture by summarizing key concepts across cancer hallmarks and closing the session.
